title: Outage Report Inspection Checklist Form
subtitle: An original outage report workflow that guides a bounded inspection from readiness through findings and release, with explicit qualified-review, stop-work, escalation, and accountable handoff controls.
description: A workflow-complete outage report inspection checklist form for the utility interruption and restoration event that captures exact identity, domain observations, supporting evidence, decisions, exceptions, responsible owners, and closeout without replacing professional judgment or the organization's controlling procedures.
use_case: Use when an assigned inspector must confirm safe observation boundaries, document domain-specific conditions, route deficiencies, and record a qualified acceptance, restriction, or follow-up decision. The outage coordination lead owns routing, and closure requires documented evidence, disposition of restrictions, and acceptance by the designated reviewer.

sections.title: Outage report inspection identity and authority
sections.guidance: Define the asset, inspection scope, qualified reviewer, and conditions before observations begin.

sections.title: Outage report readiness and safe observation boundary
sections.guidance: Confirm identity, operating context, access, and limits before checking condition.

blocks.label: Stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: This record supports situational awareness; it does not authorize switching, valve operation, entry, or approach to damaged utility equipment. Keep callers and the public away from downed lines, gas odors, flooding, fire, and unstable areas. Route emergency indicators immediately and leave isolation and restoration decisions to designated operations control and qualified crews.

sections.title: Outage report inspection points and finding evidence
sections.guidance: Check each point only when observed; use the findings table for condition, evidence, and disposition.

blocks.label: Domain inspection checklist
items: Event, service type, affected area, start time, and reporting source are identified
Duplicate reports were linked without discarding distinct safety observations
Downed lines, odor, fire, flooding, traffic, or public exposure was screened first
Critical facilities, medically dependent customers, and lifeline impacts were routed
Device, circuit, feeder, main, zone, or upstream status references were recorded
Dispatch, operations, emergency, and mutual-aid assignments are traceable
Isolation, switching, valve, or restoration authority remains with operations control
Affected-customer estimate states source, timestamp, and confidence
Crew observations separate confirmed facts from suspected cause
Public update, agency notice, and internal briefing references are logged
Partial restoration, remaining pockets, and customer callbacks are visible
Final restoration was verified and unresolved follow-up has an owner

fields.label: Inaccessible areas, sampling limits, representative conditions, trends, and supporting context

sections.title: Outage report exceptions, stop conditions, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make every unresolved condition visible with an immediate control, owner, due point, and final disposition.

blocks.label: Stop-condition screen
items: Downed or sagging conductor, arcing, fire, or damaged electrical asset
Gas odor, hissing, damaged main, regulator, or atmosphere concern
Water-main break, flooding, washout, sinkhole, or energized water exposure
Steam, pressure, chemical, traffic, debris, or unstable structure
Public entry into an uncontrolled utility work or damage zone
Unknown system state, backfeed, switching, valve, or isolation status
Critical-service consequence beyond the current response capability
Any condition requiring emergency command or operations control
blocks.guidance: Check any condition observed or reported; checking an item does not mean the condition is controlled.

blocks.label: Qualified-person and stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: This record supports situational awareness; it does not authorize switching, valve operation, entry, or approach to damaged utility equipment. Keep callers and the public away from downed lines, gas odors, flooding, fire, and unstable areas. Route emergency indicators immediately and leave isolation and restoration decisions to designated operations control and qualified crews.

blocks.label: Exception and escalation register
blocks.guidance: Link each inspection exception to supporting evidence and keep it open until disposition is recorded.

sections.title: Outage report decision, handoff, and accountable closeout
sections.guidance: Record the decision, remaining limitations, next action, and the people accountable for acceptance.

blocks.label: Closeout completeness
items: Utility interruption and restoration event identity and location were reconciled
Observed facts, measurements, and evidence references are complete
Decision authority and applicable review requirements were confirmed
Stop conditions, restrictions, and open exceptions remain visible
Customer, operations, or site handoff was recorded
Next action, owner, due point, and record-retention route are explicit

fields.label: Limitations, assumptions, restrictions, customer message, and next-action context

blocks.label: Accountable review and handoff
blocks.guidance: Signatures acknowledge the recorded decision and handoff; they do not waive unresolved restrictions.
